recipes.name: The Ultimate V60 Technique
recipes.author: James Hoffmann
recipes.grind: Medium-fine
recipes.blurb: Two big pours, one gentle stir, one swirl. The most-copied V60 recipe on the internet, and it earns it.
recipes.sourceNote: Numbers follow Hoffmann's published Ultimate V60 Technique. The wording is ours.

sources.note: The Ultimate V60 Technique video.
Written-up version of the video: 30 g / 500 g, 60 g bloom, 300 g by 1:15, 500 g by 1:45.

prep: Rinse the paper thoroughly with hot water, then dump the rinse water.
Add the grounds and shake the dripper so the bed sits flat.
Put the whole thing on the scale and zero it.
tips: The swirl after the bloom matters more than your pour pattern. Wet everything.
If drawdown finishes well before 3:30, you are grinding too coarse.
Pouring on the paper is not the sin people say it is. Pouring unevenly is.

steps.title: Bloom to 60 g
steps.detail: Pour 60 g quickly, then swirl the whole dripper until every ground is wet.

steps.title: Up to 300 g
steps.detail: Steady spiral from the centre outward. Hit 300 g by 1:15 — that is 60% of the water.

steps.title: Up to 500 g
steps.detail: Slower and more central. Finish the water by 1:45.

steps.title: Gentle stir
steps.detail: One turn clockwise, one anticlockwise. Knocks grounds off the wall.

steps.title: Swirl flat
steps.detail: Let the level drop a little, then swirl to settle the bed flat.

steps.title: Drawdown
steps.detail: Hands off. You are aiming to finish somewhere around 3:30.

recipes.name: The 4:6 Method
recipes.author: Tetsu Kasuya
recipes.grind: Coarse, a step coarser than your usual paper-filter setting
recipes.blurb: Five pours, forty-five seconds apart. The first 40% sets the balance of sweetness and acidity, the last 60% sets strength. Won the 2016 World Brewers Cup.
recipes.sourceNote: Kasuya's own numbers as published by Hario and in the Kurasu breakdown of his 2016 World Brewers Cup routine (50 / 70 split, pours every 45 s, lift at 3:30). Wording is ours. Corrected 2026-11 to match Kasuya's published 50 / 70 opening split.

sources.note: Breakdown of the 2016 World Brewers Cup routine.
Interview with Kasuya; a later variant times the last two pours at 2:10 and 2:40.

prep: Rinse the paper, add the grounds and level the bed.
Decide your split before you start. See the tips.
Coarse is not a typo. Go coarser than you normally would.
tips: The first two pours set the flavour. A smaller first pour (50 then 70) is sweeter. A bigger first pour (70 then 50) is brighter and more acidic.
The last 180 g sets strength. Split it into more pours for a stronger cup, fewer for a lighter one.
Wait for each pour to drain through before the next one.
Hario's later write-up times the last two pours at 2:10 and 2:40. Either rhythm works if you still lift at 3:30.

steps.title: Pour 1 to 50 g
steps.detail: First flavour pour. Wet everything, then let it drain through.

steps.title: Pour 2 to 120 g
steps.detail: 70 g more. That is your 40% done. Everything after this is strength.

steps.title: Pour 3 to 180 g
steps.detail: 60 g, steady and central, once the bed has drained.

steps.title: Pour 4 to 240 g
steps.detail: 60 g more. Keep the 45-second rhythm.

steps.title: Pour 5 to 300 g
steps.detail: Last 60 g. Finish the water.

steps.title: Lift at 3:30
steps.detail: Let it drip, then lift the dripper off at 3:30 even if it has not finished.

recipes.name: The Ultimate French Press
recipes.author: James Hoffmann
recipes.grind: Medium, not as coarse as you think
recipes.blurb: Break the crust, skim the foam, then wait. The plunger is a lid, not a filter.
recipes.sourceNote: Follows Hoffmann's published French press method.

sources.note: The video. Its description has no written recipe.
Aggregator write-up of the video's numbers.

prep: Preheat the press with hot water and dump it.
Add grounds, put the press on the scale, zero it.
Leave the plunger out entirely for now.
prepNoScale: Measure {water} of water in a jug.
tips: Do not plunge to the bottom. Push just below the surface and pour.
Stop pouring while there is still liquid above the sludge line.
Waiting longer than nine minutes costs you nothing but heat.

steps.title: All the water
steps.detail: Pour all 500 g straight onto the grounds in one go.

steps.title: Steep four minutes
steps.detail: Lid off, plunger out. Do nothing at all.

steps.title: Break the crust
steps.detail: Three gentle stirs through the crust. Most of it sinks.

steps.title: Skim
steps.detail: Scoop the foam and floaters off with two spoons and bin them.

steps.title: Wait it out
steps.detail: Five more minutes. The fines settle and the cup gets noticeably cleaner.

steps.title: Pour
steps.detail: Plunge to just below the surface. Pour slowly. Leave the sludge behind.

recipes.name: The Ultimate AeroPress
recipes.author: James Hoffmann
recipes.grind: The finer end of medium (for light roasts). Darker roasts: coarser, and a slightly higher dose.
recipes.blurb: Standard orientation, no stirring, one swirl. Deliberately unfussy and very hard to beat.
recipes.sourceNote: From the written summary in Hoffmann's Ultimate AeroPress Technique video description. Wording is ours. Corrected 2026-11 to match the written summary: no rinse, swirl with the plunger in, press all the way.

sources.note: Written summary in the video description.

prep: Put a paper filter in the cap. No rinsing, no preheating. Hoffmann tested it and it makes no difference.
Stand the AeroPress on the mug, add the coffee, put it all on the scale and zero it.
Bring the water to the boil and use it straight away.
prepNoScale: Stand the AeroPress on the mug and add {coffee}.
Measure {water} of water in a jug.
tips: The plunger only goes in early to stop the drip. That is its whole job here.
If pressing is a fight, grind coarser rather than pushing harder.
Darker roast? Use a little more coffee and grind coarser.

steps.title: All 200 g
steps.detail: Pour the water so it wets all the coffee as you go. No stirring.

steps.title: Plunger in, wait
steps.detail: Straight away, set the plunger about 1 cm into the top to stop the drip. Wait two minutes.

steps.title: Swirl
steps.detail: Hold the brewer and plunger together and give it a gentle swirl.

steps.title: Settle
steps.detail: Wait 30 seconds for the grounds to drop.

steps.title: Press gently, all the way
steps.detail: Steady, gentle pressure right to the bottom. The hiss at the end is fine.

recipes.name: High-Extraction AeroPress
recipes.author: Lance Hedrick
recipes.grind: Fine. Near espresso, definitely finer than V60
recipes.blurb: Grind fine, agitate hard early, press slowly. Built around pushing extraction up without the bitterness people expect.
recipes.sourceNote: ADAPTED from Hedrick's publicly described AeroPress approach: fine grind, aggressive early agitation, slow press, no bypass. These numbers are not from one Hedrick recipe. For the numbers from his 'A Very Good Aeropress Recipe' video, use "A Very Good AeroPress".
prep: Rinse the paper. Standard orientation, brewer on the mug.
Add grounds and shake the brewer to level them.
tips: The hard stir during the bloom is the point. It is what evens out a fine bed.
If the press is a fight, you have gone too fine for your filter, not too fine for the coffee.
No bypass water. Dilute in the cup afterwards if you want it longer.

steps.title: Bloom to 50 g
steps.detail: 50 g in, then stir hard for ten seconds. Really agitate it.

steps.title: Let it breathe
steps.detail: Degassing happens here. Leave it alone.

steps.title: Fill to 250 g
steps.detail: Pour the rest in fairly quickly.

steps.title: Swirl
steps.detail: Swirl to knock grounds off the walls and level the bed.

steps.title: Steep
steps.detail: Seal with the plunger and wait.

steps.title: Slow press
steps.detail: Forty-five seconds of slow, even pressure. Slow press means less channelling.

recipes.name: V60 with the Rao Spin
recipes.author: Scott Rao
recipes.grind: Medium
recipes.blurb: Spin after the bloom, one continuous pour, spin at the end. Judge the whole brew by how flat the bed is.
recipes.sourceNote: ADAPTED from Rao's widely published V60 guidance: bloom, spin, single continuous pour, terminal spin, flat bed. Not a published Rao recipe: his 2017 post shows a one-pour 22 g brew with no water weight or temperature. For his published numbers, use "V60 with the Rao Spin".

sources.note: A one-pour 22 g V60 with no water weight or temperature given.

prep: Rinse the paper well. The seal against the cone matters.
Level the bed. Zero the scale.
tips: A crater or a high-and-dry ring means the bed moved. Fix the pour, not the grind.
Do not pour down the side. Keep it central and calm.
The end spin is not optional. It is what makes the bed flat.

steps.title: Bloom to 60 g
steps.detail: Wet everything fast, then spin the dripper until there are no dry pockets.

steps.title: Continuous pour
steps.detail: One unbroken, unhurried pour to 360 g. Central, never on the wall.

steps.title: The spin
steps.detail: As the level drops, spin the dripper to flatten the bed and pull fines off the paper.

steps.title: Drawdown
steps.detail: Aim to finish around 3:00 to 3:30. Then look at the bed.

recipes.name: Light Roast Espresso
recipes.author: Lance Hedrick
recipes.grind: Espresso. Dial by taste, not by number
recipes.blurb: Long ratio, long pre-infusion, obsessive prep. Light roasts want time and gentleness, not pressure.
recipes.sourceNote: ADAPTED from Hedrick's general light-roast espresso guidance: long ratio, extended low-pressure pre-infusion, thorough WDT, puck screen. This is not a single published recipe. Dial it to your machine.
prep: Weigh 18 g into the basket. WDT thoroughly — this matters more than the tamp.
Level, tamp once, no tapping. Puck screen on top if you have one.
Purge the group. Cup on the scale, zeroed.
tips: For light roasts, 1:2.5 to 1:3 is a normal place to land, not a mistake.
Sour and thin means under-extracted: grind finer or go longer, do not just add pressure.
Change one variable per shot. Write it down before you taste.

steps.title: Pre-infusion
steps.detail: Low pressure. Let the puck saturate. First drops around 8 to 12 seconds.

steps.title: Ramp and pull
steps.detail: Full pressure. Watch the stream, not the clock. Chase 45 g.

steps.title: Stop and taste
steps.detail: Stop at yield. Taste it before you change anything.

recipes.name: Fine and Fast
recipes.author: Matt Perger
recipes.grind: Fine. Finer than feels sensible
recipes.blurb: Grind as fine as your brewer tolerates, agitate, and stop worrying about a slow drawdown. Extraction beats caution.
recipes.sourceNote: ADAPTED from Perger's long-standing public argument for finer grinding and higher extraction. This is his philosophy expressed as a recipe, not a recipe he published verbatim.

sources.note: 2012 Hario V60 video. No written recipe.

prep: Rinse paper, level bed, zero scale.
Grind a click or two finer than your usual V60 setting.
tips: Bitter AND drying is over-extraction, so back off. Bitter but sweet is usually fine.
A four to five minute drawdown is not automatically a failure.
Stir. Do not fear agitation.

steps.title: Bloom to 60 g
steps.detail: Wet fast, then stir properly. No dry grounds anywhere.

steps.title: Up to 350 g
steps.detail: Pour it all in one confident go. Keep the bed agitated.

steps.title: Stir again
steps.detail: Yes, again. Even bed, even extraction.

steps.title: Drawdown
steps.detail: Let it take as long as it takes. Judge it in the cup.

recipes.name: Low-Agitation Pulse Pour
recipes.author: Jonathan Gagné
recipes.grind: Medium-fine
recipes.blurb: Small, gentle pulses that barely disturb the bed. The opposite bet from Perger, and it also works.
recipes.sourceNote: ADAPTED, and not Gagné's own recipe: a low-agitation, Melodrip-style take on ideas he explores on Coffee ad Astra. He publishes a different V60 recipe (22 g / 352 g, three spins); use "Gagné's V60" for that.
prep: Rinse paper. Level the bed carefully — distribution is doing the work here.
If you have a Melodrip or a fine spray, use it. Otherwise pour from low and slow.
tips: The whole idea is not to churn the bed. No stirring, no hard streams.
Fines migration is the enemy and gentleness is the defence.
If it tastes under-extracted, grind finer before you pour harder.

steps.title: Gentle bloom to 55 g
steps.detail: Wet everything with as little force as you can manage.

steps.title: Pulse to 150 g
steps.detail: Slow, low pour. Stop and let it fall.

steps.title: Pulse to 250 g
steps.detail: Same again. Never let the bed go dry.

steps.title: Pulse to 360 g
steps.detail: Final pulse. No swirl, no stir.

steps.title: Drawdown
steps.detail: Hands off completely. Expect a slightly domed bed, which is fine here.

recipes.name: Chemex, Nordic Style
recipes.author: Tim Wendelboe
recipes.grind: Medium-coarse
recipes.blurb: Sixty grams per litre, slow and clean. A big transparent cup that shows off a light roast.
recipes.sourceNote: ADAPTED from Wendelboe's published brewing guidance. He publishes no Chemex recipe, and his own ratio is 65 g per litre; these numbers and timings are ours. For his method applied to a Chemex, use "Wendelboe Pour-Over, on a Chemex".

sources.note: His general pour-over method: 65 g per litre.

prep: Rinse the Chemex paper very thoroughly. Thick paper, real papery taste if you skip this.
Dump the rinse water, add grounds, level, zero.
tips: Keep the water level well below the rim of the paper.
The thick filter is slow by design. Do not chase a fast drawdown.

steps.title: Bloom to 60 g
steps.detail: Wet all the grounds and give it a gentle stir.

steps.title: Up to 250 g
steps.detail: Slow spiral, staying off the paper.

steps.title: Up to 380 g
steps.detail: Keep the level steady rather than flooding it.

steps.title: Up to 500 g
steps.detail: Finish the water.

steps.title: Drawdown
steps.detail: Expect 4:00 to 4:30 total on a Chemex. That is normal.

recipes.name: Kalita Wave 185
recipes.author: Onyx Coffee Lab
recipes.grind: Medium
recipes.blurb: Flat bed, three even pours, very repeatable. The recipe for when you want the same cup twice.
recipes.sourceNote: ADAPTED from Onyx's Kalita Wave brew guidance. Onyx's current guides do not use these numbers; for their Monarch guide, use "Kalita Wave, Onyx Style".

sources.note: Current guides are per coffee.

prep: Rinse the wave filter and seat it flat in the brewer.
Add grounds, tap level, zero the scale.
tips: The flat bottom forgives a lot. Pour into the centre and let the geometry work.
Three pours of roughly equal size is the whole trick.

steps.title: Bloom to 60 g
steps.detail: Saturate everything and give it a small swirl.

steps.title: Up to 160 g
steps.detail: Centre pour, small circles.

steps.title: Up to 260 g
steps.detail: Wait for the level to drop between pours.

steps.title: Up to 360 g
steps.detail: Final pour, finish the water.

steps.title: Drawdown
steps.detail: Target around 3:30. The bed should end up flat and even.

recipes.name: Everyday Pour-Over
recipes.author: Morgan Eckroth
recipes.grind: Medium, about coarse sand
recipes.blurb: Built for repeatability rather than heroics. The one you run every morning without thinking about it.
recipes.sourceNote: ADAPTED from Morgan Eckroth's approachable pour-over teaching (2022 US Barista Champion, @morgandrinkscoffee). This captures their emphasis — consistent technique over expensive gear, forgiving ratios, one variable at a time — rather than reproducing a single recipe they published. Edit the numbers to match whichever of their videos you are following.

sources.note: 'How I ACTUALLY Make Coffee At Home', pour-over chapter at 6:32. No written recipe.

prep: Rinse the paper and preheat the mug or carafe with the rinse water.
Add grounds, tap the dripper flat, zero the scale.
Decide now what you are changing from last time. Just the one thing.
tips: Consistency beats precision. Same kettle, same pour height, same order, every morning.
Change one variable per brew or you will never know which one did it.
A modest grinder used carefully beats an expensive one used carelessly.

steps.title: Bloom to 50 g
steps.detail: Roughly twice the weight of your coffee. Swirl until there are no dry patches.

steps.title: Up to 200 g
steps.detail: Slow spiral out and back. Keep the level steady rather than flooding it.

steps.title: Up to 350 g
steps.detail: Same rhythm again. Finish the water.

steps.title: Level it
steps.detail: One gentle swirl so the bed settles flat.

steps.title: Drawdown
steps.detail: Aim to finish around 3:15 to 3:45. Note where it actually landed.

recipes.name: Switch Hybrid: Steep and Release
recipes.author: Community standard
recipes.grind: Medium-fine
recipes.blurb: Percolate, close the valve and steep, then release. Immersion body with filter clarity.
recipes.sourceNote: The widely used Hario Switch hybrid pattern rather than one person's recipe. For named Switch recipes, see Kasuya, Fukahori and Bøen.
prep: Rinse paper. Valve OPEN to start.
Add grounds, level, zero the scale.
tips: Closing the valve earlier gives more body, later gives more clarity.
If the release is very slow, grind coarser. A stalled Switch is a bitter Switch.

steps.title: Valve open, bloom to 60 g
steps.detail: Open valve. Bloom and swirl.

steps.title: Up to 300 g, then CLOSE
steps.detail: Pour the rest, then shut the valve to start the immersion.

steps.title: Steep
steps.detail: Closed valve. Let it sit. This is where the body comes from.

steps.title: Swirl and OPEN
steps.detail: Gentle swirl, then open the valve.

steps.title: Release
steps.detail: Let it drain fully. Around 3:30 to 4:00 total.

recipes.name: Moka Pot, Properly
recipes.author: James Hoffmann
recipes.grind: Fine-medium, about table salt
recipes.blurb: Pre-boiled water and low heat. Almost all moka pot bitterness is scorched coffee, not strong coffee.
recipes.sourceNote: Follows the technique from Hoffmann's moka pot videos. In the series the dose is a level, untamped basket, not grams: 17 g and 150 g are our numbers for a three-cup pot.

sources.note: Ultimate Moka Pot Technique. The description has no written recipe.

prep: Boil a kettle first. The boiler gets pre-boiled water, never cold water.
Fill the boiler to just below the safety valve.
Level the basket without tamping. Assemble with a towel, it is hot.
tips: Lid open so you can watch the stream. It should be honey-coloured and steady.
The moment it goes pale and sputters, pull it and cool the base.

steps.title: Low heat
steps.detail: Smallest burner, low heat. Wait for the first coffee to appear.

steps.title: The stream
steps.detail: Steady dark stream. Keep the heat low, do not let it roar.

steps.title: Kill it
steps.detail: At the first pale sputter: off the heat, base into cold water.

recipes.name: A Better 1-Cup V60
recipes.author: James Hoffmann
recipes.grind: Medium-fine
recipes.blurb: Five small, even pours instead of two big ones. Hoffmann's fix for the single cup, where a small bed drains too fast for the classic method.
recipes.sourceNote: Dose, water, grind and every timing come from the written recipe in Hoffmann's video description. Wording is ours.
prep: Use soft, filtered water, freshly boiled for lighter roasts.
Rinse the paper, add the coffee and level the bed.
Zero the scale.
tips: Each pour is 50 g, a fifth of the brew. Small and even is the whole idea.
Expect to finish around 3:00, but taste beats the clock.
There is a follow-up video answering common questions: https://youtu.be/v5WQ1sZzW4o

steps.title: Bloom with 50 g
steps.detail: Pour 50 g. At about 0:10 give it a gentle swirl, then leave it until 0:45.

steps.title: Up to 100 g
steps.detail: Pour to 100 g by 1:00, then pause.

steps.title: Up to 150 g
steps.detail: At 1:10 pour to 150 g by 1:20, then pause.

steps.title: Up to 200 g
steps.detail: At 1:30 pour to 200 g by 1:40, then pause.

steps.title: Up to 250 g
steps.detail: At 1:50 pour the last 50 g, finishing by 2:00.

steps.title: Gentle swirl
steps.detail: One gentle swirl to flatten the bed.

steps.title: Drawdown
steps.detail: Should finish around 3:00. Some variance is normal.

recipes.name: Immersion Iced Coffee
recipes.author: James Hoffmann
recipes.grind: Finer than your pour-over setting, but nowhere near espresso
recipes.blurb: Steep hot and strong, then strain straight onto ice. Easier than iced pour-over, and the long steep keeps it sweet.
recipes.sourceNote: From the step-by-step and ratio table in Hoffmann's video description. 330 g is the hot water. 170 g of ice comes on top, for 75 g per litre (about 1:13) overall. Any immersion brewer works; a Clever-style dripper is used here.
prep: Preheat the brewer.
Put 170 g of ice, straight from the freezer, in the carafe.
One cup instead: 19 g coffee, 165 g hot water, 85 g ice.
tips: Depending on the brewer, add coffee then water, or water then coffee. Both work.
The amounts are flexible. Ice cubes are never a neat size.
Darker roasts can steep 4 minutes instead of 5.

steps.title: 330 g of hot water
steps.detail: Add the coffee and 330 g of freshly boiled, clean, soft water (or water first, then coffee).

steps.title: No dry pockets
steps.detail: Make sure everything is mixed and no dry clumps remain.

steps.title: Steep 5 minutes
steps.detail: At least 5 minutes, or 4 for darker roasts.

steps.title: Strain onto the ice
steps.detail: Set the brewer on the carafe of ice and let it drain.

steps.title: Stir and serve
steps.detail: Stir in any ice that is left, then serve over fresh ice.

recipes.name: Cold Brew, No Filtering
recipes.author: James Hoffmann
recipes.grind: Fine, like a moka pot or AeroPress setting (about a 250 micron burr gap). If unsure, err finer.
recipes.blurb: Fine grind, hard stir, twelve hours in the fridge, then just pour it off. No filter, no sludge, no fuss.
recipes.sourceNote: From the written recipe in Hoffmann's 'Everything I Learned About Cold Brew' video description. He gives 'room temperature' water; 20 °C is our stand-in. The 250 micron figure is a burr gap, not a particle size.
prep: Use water you would happily brew filter coffee with, at room temperature.
Optional: 10 drops of a beer fining agent (he used Mangrove Jack's Liquid Beer Finings) to help the grounds settle.
You need a container with a lid that fits in the fridge.
tips: This is a ready-to-drink strength, not a concentrate.
Be heavy-handed with the stir. Everything needs to be wet.
Stop pouring as you get close to the sediment.

steps.title: All the water
steps.detail: Add 1 litre of room-temperature water to the grounds.

steps.title: Stir hard
steps.detail: Stir until everything is completely mixed. Add the fining agent now if using it.

steps.title: 12 hours in the fridge
steps.detail: Lid on, into the fridge, and leave it so the grounds settle.

steps.title: Pour it off
steps.detail: Gently pour the liquid into a carafe, stopping before the sediment.

recipes.name: Switch Hybrid (the 'Devil' Recipe)
recipes.author: Tetsu Kasuya
recipes.grind: Medium-fine, a touch finer than your pour-over setting. Adjust so the brew takes 3:00.
recipes.blurb: Percolate with hot water first, then close the valve and steep the rest in 70 °C water. Sweet and round, with the bitterness kept out.
recipes.sourceNote: Kasuya's Switch recipe as reported by two aggregators, neither of which links to Kasuya's own source: Outpost Coffee and Honest Coffee Guide (https://honestcoffeeguide.com/brew-recipes/tetsu-kasuya-hybrid-method). Both give 20 g / 280 g, two 60 g open-valve pours, then 160 g of 70 °C water with the valve closed, about 3:00 total. Outpost gives 90-95 °C for the first pours and a 30 s steep; Honest Coffee Guide gives 93 °C and a 10 s steep. The steps follow Outpost. We could not read Kasuya's own video.
prep: Rinse the paper, then add the coffee and shake it flat.
Valve OPEN to start.
Plan how you will get to 70 °C quickly: a second kettle, or a splash of cold water into the first.
tips: Two temperatures are the trick: hot for the first 120 g, 70 °C for the immersion.
Adjust the grind so the whole thing lands at about 3:00.
Too strong? Add a little hot water to the cup at the end.
Honest Coffee Guide's version steeps only 10 s and closes the valve again at about 3:00, even if it has not finished draining.

steps.title: Valve open, 60 g
steps.detail: Pour 60 g of hot water, wet everything evenly, and let it drain for 30 seconds.

steps.title: Valve open, up to 120 g
steps.detail: Another 60 g. Let it drain for about 45 seconds while you cool the kettle to 70 °C.

steps.title: CLOSE, 160 g at 70 °C
steps.detail: Close the valve and pour 160 g of 70 °C water.

steps.title: Steep 30 s
steps.detail: Valve closed. Leave it for about 30 seconds.

steps.title: OPEN and drain
steps.detail: Open the valve and let it drain. About 3:00 total.

recipes.name: Easy Hario Switch
recipes.author: Emi Fukahori
recipes.grind: 25 clicks on a Comandante C40. She gives no other grind measure.
recipes.blurb: A closed-valve bloom, then one continuous centre pour. The house Switch recipe at MAME, from the 2018 World Brewers Cup champion.
recipes.sourceNote: From Fukahori's recipe as written in the European Coffee Trip video description, filmed with her: 14 g, 200 g at 93 °C, 25 clicks on a Comandante, 50 g closed-valve bloom, open at 0:30, one 150 g centre pour finished by 1:10, 2:20 total. Wording is ours.
prep: Rinse a V60 02 paper in the Switch.
Add the coffee, level it, zero the scale.
Valve CLOSED to start.
tips: One single, continuous pour into the centre. No pulses.
This is the recipe used across MAME's shops in Switzerland.

steps.title: Valve closed, 50 g
steps.detail: Pour 50 g with the valve closed. Let it bloom.

steps.title: OPEN, 150 g centre pour
steps.detail: Open the valve at 0:30 and pour 150 g in one steady stream into the centre. Done by 1:10.

steps.title: Drawdown
steps.detail: Let it drain. About 2:20 total.

recipes.name: Switch, Closed-Open-Closed
recipes.author: Ole Kristian Bøen
recipes.grind: Medium-fine
recipes.blurb: Bloom closed, pour open, steep closed, release. The recipe the 2020 Norwegian Brewers Cup champion took to the 2021 World Brewers Cup.
recipes.sourceNote: From Bøen's recipe published by Hario Europe. Wording is ours.
prep: Rinse a paper in a Switch 02.
Add the coffee, level it, zero the scale.
Valve CLOSED to start.
tips: The valve flips three times. Say each move out loud the first time.
He brewed a natural Geisha from Hacienda La Esmeralda with it in Milan.

steps.title: Closed, 50 g
steps.detail: Valve closed. Pour 50 g and bloom until 0:40.

steps.title: OPEN, 100 g centre
steps.detail: Open the valve and pour 100 g into the centre.

steps.title: CLOSE, 90 g circles
steps.detail: At 1:30 close the valve and pour 90 g in circles.

steps.title: OPEN and drain
steps.detail: At 2:10 open the valve and let it run. 3:00 to 3:15 total.

recipes.name: Five-Pour V60
recipes.author: Matt Winton
recipes.grind: Coarse. Winton says he ground quite coarse, around 3.6 on his Kinu M47.
recipes.blurb: Five equal pours, thirty seconds apart, no stirring. The 2021 World Brewers Cup winner, about as simple as a championship recipe gets.
recipes.sourceNote: Hario's video with Winton has no written recipe and could not be read. 20 g / 300 g, 93 °C then 88 °C, a metal V60, a Kinu M47, five pours and a 2:40 finish come from Wikipedia's World Brewers Cup table (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Brewers_Cup, an aggregator citing the SCA rankings and a Barista Hustle interview with him). recipes.name: WAC 2019 Winner
recipes.author: Wendelien van Bunnik
recipes.grind: Mahlkönig EK43S. The archive rates the grind 7 on a 1-10 scale (1 very fine, 10 very coarse).
recipes.blurb: A big 30 g dose, firm stirs, a fast concentrate, then diluted to taste. Winner of the 2019 World AeroPress Championship (Netherlands).
recipes.sourceNote: From the official World AeroPress Championship recipe archive. The water total is 100 g brew water plus 120 g dilution (her final amount).
prep: Inverted AeroPress, Aesir filter, rinsed.
Soft water: she used Spa Blauw at about 30 ppm.
tips: She cooled the cup to about 60 °C by stirring and decanting before serving.
Dilute to taste. 100 g is the starting point, 120 g was her final.

steps.title: 100 g in 10 s
steps.detail: Pour 100 g over the coffee in 10 seconds.

steps.title: 20 firm stirs
steps.detail: Stir firmly 20 times in 10 seconds.

steps.title: Cap on
steps.detail: Fit the cap with the rinsed filter and gently press out the air.

steps.title: Flip and press
steps.detail: At 0:40 flip and press out all the coffee. About 60 g of extract.

steps.title: Dilute
steps.detail: Add 100 g of water, then more to taste. She used 120 g, 220 g of water in all. Cool to about 60 °C by stirring and decanting.

recipes.name: WAC 2018 Winner
recipes.author: Carolina Ibarra Garay
recipes.grind: Mahlkönig EK43S. The archive rates the grind 8 on a 1-10 scale (1 very fine, 10 very coarse).
recipes.blurb: A huge dose, a 30-second chopstick stir and a concentrate topped with hot and cool water. Winner of the 2018 World AeroPress Championship (USA).
recipes.sourceNote: From the official World AeroPress Championship recipe archive, where she is listed as Carolina Garay (USA).
prep: Inverted AeroPress, paper filter rinsed with hot water.
Brita-filtered water at 85 °C.
Do not preheat the server.
tips: Wooden chopsticks for the stir: vigorous but careful.

steps.title: 100 g over 30 s
steps.detail: Pour 100 g of 85 °C water over 30 seconds.

steps.title: Chopstick stir
steps.detail: Stir vigorously but carefully for 30 seconds.

steps.title: Cap, flip, press
steps.detail: Fit the cap, flip, and press into a glass server for 30 seconds.

steps.title: Top up
steps.detail: Add 60 g of 85 °C water and 40 g of room-temperature water.

recipes.name: WAC 2017 Winner
recipes.author: Paulina Miczka
recipes.grind: Grinder not named. The archive rates the grind 8 on a 1-10 scale (1 very fine, 10 very coarse).
recipes.blurb: A 35 g dose, 150 g of water, continuous stirring, then a strong concentrate opened up with hot water. Winner of the 2017 World AeroPress Championship (England).
recipes.sourceNote: From the official World AeroPress Championship recipe archive. The archive lists 370 g of water in total; the steps add up to 150 g brew water plus 160-200 g hot water, so the water total uses 150 + 200.
prep: Inverted AeroPress, paper filter, pre-wet.
Water at 84 °C.
tips: The concentrate is about 4.5% TDS. Dilute to taste within 160-200 g.
Hoffmann links her technique in his Ultimate AeroPress video description.

steps.title: 150 g
steps.detail: Pour 150 g in 15 seconds.

steps.title: Stir continuously
steps.detail: Keep stirring until 0:35.

steps.title: Cap on
steps.detail: Fit the pre-wet cap at 0:35 and wait.

steps.title: Flip and press
steps.detail: Flip at 1:05 and press until 1:35. About 90 ml of concentrate.

steps.title: Dilute
steps.detail: Add 160-200 g of hot water to taste. 200 g makes 350 g of water in all.

recipes.name: A Very Good AeroPress
recipes.author: Lance Hedrick
recipes.grind: Medium-fine, finer than pour-over. Start coarser and step finer.
recipes.blurb: Gentle bloom, a swirl instead of a stir, and a slow press that stops before the hiss. Clean and sweet without fuss.
recipes.sourceNote: From Hedrick's 'A Very Good Aeropress Recipe, Maybe the Best' as transcribed by AeroPrecipe (an aggregator). We could not read the video itself. The bloom amount is not given, so pour just enough to wet the bed.
prep: Paper filter in the cap. Standard orientation, brewer on the mug.
Add the coffee and level the bed. Zero the scale.
Light roast: 15 g. Medium: 16 g. Dark: 17 g.
tips: Hedrick never brews above 95 °C: about 90-92 °C for light roasts, 88 °C for medium, 82-84 °C for dark.
A slow press gives a cleaner cup with better texture.
Coarser grind? Just let it sit longer before pressing.
Do not reheat the kettle between pours.

steps.title: Gentle bloom
steps.detail: Pour slowly, just enough to wet all the coffee without driving water deep into the bed. Swirl, then wait.

steps.title: Up to 250 g
steps.detail: Pour the rest of the water normally.

steps.title: Plunger on
steps.detail: Set the plunger on top to stop the drip.

steps.title: Swirl
steps.detail: Lift it off the scale and give it a swirl.

steps.title: Wait until 2:00
steps.detail: Longer extracts a bit more, with diminishing returns.

steps.title: Press gently
steps.detail: Slow and gentle. Stop before you press through the hiss.

recipes.name: A classic double
recipes.author: 3FE
recipes.grind: Fine
recipes.blurb: The textbook double: 18 g in, 36 g out, in 25 to 30 seconds. A sensible first shot on any machine.
recipes.sourceNote: Numbers from 3FE's espresso brew guide: 18 g in, 36 g out in 25 to 30 seconds, machine at 93 °C. The guide's recipe box also lists 230 g of water and 30 minutes, which don't match its own steps; we follow the steps. The wording is ours.

sources.note: Espresso brew guide: 18 g dose, 36 g yield, 25-30 seconds, 93 °C, fine grind. Checked 2026-11-19.

prep: Preheat the machine until the water is at 93 °C.
Flush the group head, then empty and wipe the portafilter.
Weigh 18 g of coffee into the basket and spread it evenly.
Tamp evenly and firmly on a flat surface. Wipe loose grounds off the rim.
tips: Aim for 25 to 30 seconds. If the shot runs fast or slow, change the grind, not the dose.
Change one thing per shot, and write it down before you taste.

steps.title: Pull to 36 g
steps.detail: Lock the portafilter in and start the shot straight away. Stop at 36 g in the cup, 25 to 30 seconds in.

recipes.name: Batch brew in a drip machine
recipes.author: Allpress Espresso
recipes.grind: Medium-coarse, like rough sand or sea salt
recipes.blurb: A full pot from a filter machine: 70 g of coffee to 1.25 litres, a short bloom and one light stir.
recipes.sourceNote: Allpress's Moccamaster recipe: 70 g (about 14 tablespoons) to 1.25 litres of cold water, medium-coarse, a 30-second bloom with the slide gate closed, one light stir once the coffee is covered, about 5 to 6 minutes in all. The machine heats the water itself: SCA-certified home brewers must hold 92-96 °C, and 94 °C is the middle of that, not Allpress's number. The 5:30 finish is the middle of their 5 to 6 minutes.

sources.note: Large batch: 70 g (approx. 14 tbsp) freshly ground, medium-coarse, 1.25 l cold filtered water, 30 s bloom, light stir, about 5-6 minutes.
55-60 g of ground coffee per litre, or two tablespoons per 6 oz of water; medium-coarse, 500-800 microns.
SCA home brewer certification: water at the grounds 92-96 °C, contact time 4 to 8 minutes at full capacity.

prep: Put a paper filter in the basket and rinse it with water.
Add the coffee and shake the basket so the bed is level.
Fill the tank with cold, filtered water.
tips: Turn the machine off once the tank is empty, so the pot doesn't sit on the hot plate.
For a smaller pot keep the ratio: Moccamaster says 55 to 60 g of coffee per litre, or two tablespoons per 6 oz of water.
Brewing a lot? Grind a little coarser.

steps.title: Switch on, wait 30 seconds
steps.detail: If your machine has a drip-stop or slide gate, keep it closed for the first 30 seconds so the coffee blooms. Without one, just let it run.

steps.title: Let it brew
steps.detail: Open the gate. Once the coffee is covered with water, give it one light stir to break up dry spots. The whole pot takes about 5 to 6 minutes.

recipes.name: Vietnamese phin
recipes.author: Copper Cow Coffee
recipes.grind: Medium-fine, a little finer than pour-over
recipes.blurb: A one-cup phin: about two tablespoons of coffee, a one-minute bloom, then let it drip for 3 to 5 minutes.
recipes.sourceNote: Copper Cow's phin guide: 14 g (about 2 tablespoons) for a single-serve phin, about 1 oz of water to bloom for 60 seconds, about 4 oz of water in all, 190-205 °F, 3 to 5 minutes to brew. We read the 4 oz as the whole fill (120 g), take 93 °C from the middle of their range and give the top-up pour 30 seconds; the drip ends at 5 minutes, the top of their range.

sources.note: How to use a phin: 14 g or about 2 tablespoons, medium-fine (ground coffee: medium or universal), 1 oz bloom for 60 seconds, about 4 oz of water, 190-205 °F, 3-5 minutes.

prep: Set the phin's plate and chamber on your cup or glass.
Add the coffee, shake it level and rest the filter insert on top. No need to press.
tips: Dripping through in well under 3 minutes means go finer; much longer than 5, coarser.
Pre-ground works: Copper Cow says a medium or universal grind is fine.

steps.title: Bloom with 30 g
steps.detail: Pour about 30 g of hot water over the coffee and wait a minute.

steps.title: Fill the phin
steps.detail: Top up with the rest of the water and put the lid on.

steps.title: Let it drip
steps.detail: Leave it alone. It takes 3 to 5 minutes to drip through.

recipes.name: Cezve in two and a half minutes
recipes.author: Tetiana Tarykina
recipes.grind: Turkish: finer than espresso, like flour
recipes.blurb: A small, strong cezve on medium-high heat with three stirs, poured the moment it foams.
recipes.sourceNote: Tarykina's recipe as Fresh Cup reported it: 7.5 g of Turkish-ground coffee, 60 ml of water, medium-high heat, stirs at 0:30, 1:00 and 1:30, poured when it starts to foam, 2:30 in all. She was the 2019 Ukrainian Cezve/Ibrik Champion. She gives no water temperature: the water goes in cold, as in Copenhagen Coffee Lab's guide, and the 20 °C is ours.

sources.note: Tetiana Tarykina's cezve recipe: 7.5 g, 60 ml, medium-high heat, stir at 0:30, 1:00 and 1:30, pour when it foams, 2:30 total.
Cold, fresh water; a grind like flour; take it off before it boils over; let the grounds settle for a minute before drinking.

prep: Turkish-ground coffee: finer than espresso. Most shops sell it ready ground.
If you take sugar, add it now, with the coffee.
tips: Never let it boil over: pour as soon as the foam rises.
Let the grounds settle for a minute before you drink.

steps.title: Coffee and water in, heat on
steps.detail: Put the coffee and 60 g of cold water in the cezve and set it on medium-high heat.

steps.title: Stir
steps.detail: A short stir to wet all the coffee.

steps.title: Stir again
steps.detail: Another short stir. Keep it on the heat.

steps.title: Stir, then pour as it foams
steps.detail: One last stir. When the foam starts to rise, pour it into the cup, foam first.

recipes.name: Syphon
recipes.author: Hario
recipes.grind: Medium-fine
recipes.blurb: Hario's own syphon method: water up, coffee in, a few stirs, 70 seconds, heat off and three more stirs.
recipes.sourceNote: Hario UK's syphon guide: 17 g medium-fine to 250 g of water (15 to 17 g per 250 g works), 3 to 5 circular stirs, heat turned down to hold the water up, heat off after 70 seconds and 3 good stirs, then it drains. The water is brought to the boil in the bowl, hence 100 °C. Hario gives no time for the last stirs or the drain: the 10 and 60 seconds are ours, so finish when it has drained.

sources.note: Syphon brew guide: 17 g medium-fine, 250 g water, 3-5 circular stirs, 70 seconds, then heat off and 3 stirs.

prep: Soak the cloth filter in warm water, set it in the upper chamber and hook the chain to the bottom of the funnel.
Fill the lower bowl with hot, filtered water and light the burner.
Rest the upper chamber in the bowl at an angle; when the water boils, seat it firmly.
Start the timer once the water has risen into the upper chamber.
tips: Three to five stirs is plenty. Hario warns against stirring too much.
Let it cool a little before you drink it.

steps.title: Coffee in, stir, steep
steps.detail: Add the coffee and give it 3 to 5 circular stirs. Turn the burner down so the water just stays up.

steps.title: Heat off, three stirs
steps.detail: Turn the heat off completely and give it 3 good stirs.

steps.title: Let it drain
steps.detail: The coffee drains into the bowl. Lift off the upper chamber when it's done.

recipes.name: South Indian filter decoction
recipes.author: Blue Tokai
recipes.grind: South Indian filter grind, as sold for the filter
recipes.blurb: A strong decoction that drips for ten minutes, for two or three cups with hot milk.
recipes.sourceNote: Blue Tokai's South Indian filter guide: 18 g (about 9 teaspoons), levelled with the plunger and no pressure, 100 ml at 95 °C (about 1½ minutes off the boil), lid on, 9½ to 10 minutes to drip; then 50 ml of decoction with 60 ml of hot milk or 50 ml of hot water. The 30 seconds for the pour are ours and count inside their 10 minutes.

sources.note: South Indian filter guide: 18 g, 100 ml at 95 °C, lid on, 9.5-10 minutes; 50 ml decoction to 60 ml hot milk.

prep: Put the coffee in the upper chamber and set it on the lower one.
Level the coffee with the plunger and leave the plunger resting on top. No pressure.
tips: For a cup: 50 ml of decoction with 60 ml of hot milk, or with 50 ml of hot water. Sugar to taste.
Pour it back and forth between two cups from a height for a foamy top.
One decoction makes 2 to 3 cups and keeps in the fridge for 3 days.

steps.title: Pour 100 g at 95 °C
steps.detail: Water about a minute and a half off the boil, poured into the top chamber over the plunger.

steps.title: Lid on, let it drip
steps.detail: Keep the lid on the whole time to hold the heat. It takes 9½ to 10 minutes.
